title: Cough
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with high fever, cough (initially dry then productive), dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, and extrapulmonary symptoms: GI (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain), hyponatremia (classic lab finding), confusion/AMS, relative bradycardia. History: exposure to contaminated water sources (hot tubs, cooling towers, hotel, cruise ship). Legionella is an atypical pneumonia — intracellular pathogen not seen on Gram stain. Diagnosis: urinary antigen test (detects L. pneumophila serogroup 1 — most common, rapid), sputum culture on specialized media (BCYE agar), PCR. Severe cases require hospitalization. Treatment: macrolides (azithromycin) or respiratory fluoroquinolones (levofloxacin, moxifloxacin). Doxycycline as alternative. Treatment duration 7-14 days (longer if immunocompromised). Report to public health (Legionnaires disease is reportable).
chief_complaint: High fever, cough, GI symptoms, hyponatremia
